entries.title: a semantic search writes no vector of a second model
entries.summary: After a change of embedding model, one semantic search_symbols on a repo with a new symbol wrote that symbol's vector at the new width beside the old ones; the mixed store then scored nothing semantically and called the provider again on every search. The search now compares what built the stored vectors before it writes. On a mismatch it writes nothing, ranks without the semantic channel and returns semantic_store_mismatch with the reason; run embed_repo to rebuild. One store changes on upgrade: vectors with no metadata (left by a full re-index before 1.108.331) are no longer scored until embed_repo runs.

entries.title: the parse budget stops a slow parse again on a fresh install
entries.summary: A fresh install could resolve tree-sitter 0.26.0, which removed the attribute the per-file parse budget uses to stop a slow parse; indexing then printed 'the installed tree-sitter has no Parser.timeout_micros' and a slow file ran to its end. The dependency is now tree-sitter>=0.25,<0.26, so upgrading jcodemunch-mcp restores the stop. Also: after indexing, init printed '? files, ? symbols'; it now prints the real counts, and says 'indexing failed' with the reason when the indexer refused. And three more inputs gave a dbt or Jinja/Twig macro the wrong docstring; an existing index re-parses once at its next index run. Thanks to Dave for the report.

entries.title: a macro's docstring is the comment directly above it
entries.summary: A dbt macro, test, snapshot or materialization, and a Jinja or Twig macro or block, takes the {# comment #} above it as its docstring. In a file of documented macros every one after the first carried the FIRST comment of the file, so a search by what a macro does found the wrong macro. Each now takes the comment that ends directly above it, and the marks of a whitespace-control comment ({#- ... -#}) are no longer part of the text. An existing index re-parses once at its next index run to pick this up. Also: three loops on the parse path take time proportional to the file; a Python file of 6250 functions and 20000 module-level calls that took 63.877 s to index takes 0.593 s, with the same symbols.

entries.title: a full re-index keeps the embedding metadata beside its vectors
entries.summary: A full re-index cleared the table where the embedding store records which model, dimension and task type produced its vectors, and kept the vectors. A semantic search after a model change could then leave vectors of two widths under the new model's name, and embed_repo re-embedded the whole corpus after every full re-index. The save now keeps the embedding store's rows, so a model change after a full re-index is detected and named, and embed_repo embeds only the symbols that have no vector. Pass force=true to refresh every vector (#522, @lsg1103275794). Also: a large Vue or Svelte <script> is indexed in time proportional to its size; a 6000-function script that took over 20 seconds to parse now takes a fraction of a second, with the same symbols. Also: embed_repo no longer re-embeds a corpus for a task-type row that was never written, and names the reason when it does rebuild (#523, @lsg1103275794).
